facts.label: Analysis by dimension
facts.text: Leverage is high and swings with the political cycle rather than with debt paydown. Total debt was 5.02x derived reported EBITDA at FY2024, 9.13x at FY2025 and 8.68x on the twelve months to 2026-06-30, while carrying-value debt moved only from USD 5,621 million to USD 5,744 million and USD 5,808 million. The swing came from EBITDA, which fell from USD 1,120 million to USD 629 million as political advertising revenue dropped from USD 497 million to USD 42 million, and recovered to USD 669 million on the twelve months to 2026-06-30 with USD 113 million of political revenue in the first half of 2026. A large share of broadcasting operating expenses is fixed, so lost political revenue falls straight through to EBITDA, and creditors should expect year-end leverage to look better or worse by several turns depending on the political calendar. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 48-49; calculation K21; calculation K2; calculation K3; calculation K6

The consolidated total net leverage ratio of 5.73x at 2026-06-30 divides USD 5,696 million of net debt by a USD 994 million denominator that averages eight quarters, whose eight-quarter total of USD 1,987 million includes USD 144 million of adjustments for acquired and divested stations, financings and expected synergies, against USD 669 million of derived twelve-month EBITDA, and the first lien test of 2.55x is far below its 4.25x limit applying when the revolver is drawn. This is the strongest contrary evidence to the high-leverage reading: if political-year EBITDA in the second half of 2026 restores the twelve-month figure towards the covenant denominator, the gap would narrow, but the filings give no basis to treat the adjustments as realised. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case for lower risk is what the sources do not show: no financial sponsor, no covenant waiver or forbearance, no exchange offer or priming transaction, no fees paid to insiders and no related-party leakage appear in them, and the 2025 refinancing removed near-term maturities while the repurchases at par and the USD 250 million authorisation reduce debt. The auditor's unqualified opinions and quarterly covenant reporting add to that. These absences are not proof, because the proxy statement, the credit agreement and the indentures were not supplied. The view would move to low if the proxy statement showed a limited insider stake and a majority of independent directors and the indentures showed tight restricted-payment and unrestricted-subsidiary limits. It would move to high if the Class A votes proved to sit with one insider group and distributions, preferred repurchases or par buybacks of selected notes continued while the first lien test was tightening, or if a later filing disclosed an uptier, drop-down or non-pro-rata exchange. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 37-38, 68-70; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 25-26, 35; calculation A18

facts.text: The risk level is driven by concentrated Class A voting control and by distributions, a debt-funded preferred repurchase and acquisitions made while leverage is high, because those choices move cash and priority toward equity holders and add debt before the earnings it buys are shown, which implies higher refinancing and recovery risk for junior secured and unsecured creditors. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case for a better view is timing. Twelve-month EBITDA includes only the first half of a political year; the issuer guides third-quarter 2026 revenue to USD 935 million to USD 965 million against USD 749 million a year earlier, with political advertising of USD 165 million to USD 185 million against USD 8 million, and net retransmission revenue rose to USD 292 million from USD 281 million in the first half. The covenant ratio of 5.73x sits 1.27x below its 7.00x incurrence limit, the first lien ratio of 2.55x is far below the 4.25x limit that applies when the revolver is drawn, and management places the first maturity after the 2028 election cycle, when earnings should be at a peak. If twelve-month derived EBITDA at the end of 2026 moved back toward the USD 1,120 million of the last political year and the 2028 maturities were refinanced early, net leverage would move toward the 4.90x seen at the end of 2024 and the view would improve. It would worsen if the next off-year repeated the USD 629 million of 2025, if retransmission revenue fell faster than network fees, or if further debt-funded distributions or a covenant-limited refinancing left less room before 2028. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 1-6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 35, 37; calculation B1; calculation B13; calculation B17

facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Gray Media owns local television stations in more than a hundred US markets that reach about 37% of US television households, with the top-rated station in most of the markets Nielsen measures, plus a small production and studio business. Revenue comes in roughly equal parts from advertising and from fees that cable, satellite and streaming distributors pay to carry its stations, and political advertising adds a large layer every second year. Retransmission contracts and network affiliation agreements run for years, which gives cash-flow visibility, but advertising is sold on short contracts and the political layer disappears in odd years, so debt service in an off-year rests on a smaller, fee-based core. The group is also changing shape: it closed station purchases of USD 280 million in the first half of 2026 and swapped stations with a peer, so the earnings base is being rebuilt faster than the filings show. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 9; calculation B15; calculation B19

facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: Gray is a public company controlled through votes, not through a sponsor: ten-vote Class A shares held 51.45% of votes on 2026-07-31, and an insider family group is described as able to exert significant influence. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Volume is set by audience share and by the number of distributor subscribers, and price by the rates in retransmission contracts and advertising rate cards. Retransmission rates rise with each renewal, but subscriber losses, an Atlanta affiliation change and a satellite blackout from March to May 2026 contributed to a USD 50 million fall in first-half retransmission revenue; core advertising was flat and carries two cyclical categories, services at 26% and automotive at 17% of 2025 core advertising. Revenue is therefore cyclical, partly structurally declining in its fee line and not concentrated by customer or market; the consequence is that pricing power exists in carriage negotiations but is being spent offsetting subscriber decline, which limits growth in the cash that supports debt. Retransmission rates rise with each renewal, but subscriber losses, an Atlanta affiliation change and a satellite blackout from March to May 2026 contributed to a USD 50 million fall in first-half retransmission revenue; core advertising was flat and carries two cyclical categories, services at 26% and automotive at 17% of 2025 core advertising. Revenue is therefore cyclical, partly structurally declining in its fee line and not concentrated by customer or market; the consequence is that pricing power exists in carriage negotiations but is being spent offsetting subscriber decline, which limits growth in the cash that supports debt.

facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Network affiliation fees, compensation, benefits and programming are the main costs, and a large portion is fixed. The result is operating leverage: from 2024 to 2025 broadcasting expenses fell only USD 78 million against a USD 549 million fall in revenue, and adjusted EBITDA fell 42.3%. Margins can be partly defended through network fees, which fell USD 50 million in 2025 and fell further in the first half of 2026 as an Atlanta station went independent, but not against a political-year swing, so margin resilience is weak across the cycle and adequate within it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 48-50; EX-99.1_2026-02-26_ex_924265.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation B9

facts.text: Capital intensity is low outside construction: purchases of property and equipment were USD 108 million in 2025, USD 104 million over the last twelve months, and the issuer guides USD 120 million to USD 130 million for 2026. Conversion of EBITDA to free cash flow is volatile, with free cash flow of USD 608 million in FY2024, USD 181 million in FY2025 and USD 146 million over the last twelve months, because cash interest of about USD 385 million and cash taxes absorb most of an off-year's EBITDA. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry from cable networks, streaming and digital platforms takes advertising and audience, and cord cutting removes the subscribers who generate fees, so rivalry works on both revenue lines; local news and sports programming are the issuer's response. Distributors have bargaining power, shown by the March to May 2026 satellite blackout, while networks hold supplier power over 61.7% of retransmission revenue through affiliation fees. New entry is limited by scarce licences, but substitutes are close: advertisers can move spend to digital platforms, and viewers to streaming. The credit consequence is that pricing power in the fee line is shared with networks and contested by distributors, so net retransmission revenue is a more reliable guide to cash flow than gross revenue. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 11-13, 31; 10-Q_2026-03-31_gtn20260331_10q.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation B10

facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months, 2026 is a political year, so revenue and earnings should rise: the issuer guides third-quarter revenue to USD 935 million to USD 965 million, and 2027 is an off-year when political revenue falls back and the derived leverage figures will look worst again. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The downside is a second off-year that repeats the conditions of 2025. The initiating condition is political revenue falling back from USD 113 million in the first half of 2026 toward the USD 42 million of 2025, with retransmission revenue still falling and no new carriage gains. The first break is operational: fixed costs mean that a revenue fall of 15.1% cut adjusted EBITDA by 42.3% in 2025. The financial transmission follows from the 2025 outcome: derived EBITDA of USD 629 million against cash interest of USD 393 million is cover of 1.60x and total debt to EBITDA of 9.13x, and free cash flow of USD 181 million less USD 85 million of dividends leaves USD 96 million. Liquidity does not break in this scenario, because cash flow stays positive after dividends and USD 921 million of cash and undrawn revolver and no principal before December 2028 remain, so the consequence falls on leverage and refinancing: the 2028 and 2029 maturities would then be refinanced from a weak base, with the first lien test at 2.55x still far below its limit. Management levers are cutting capital expenditure, suspending the common dividend of USD 33 million a year, and using the USD 250 million repurchase authorisation selectively; the preferred dividend of USD 50 million a year is mandatory unless paid in kind, which blocks junior distributions. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity event through 2027 on this evidence, not to avoid a harder refinancing, and the scenario uses the pre-acquisition perimeter because purchased earnings are not disclosed. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Gray Media presents a strong-in-scale but cyclical business profile supported by local market leadership, a long runway to its first maturity and USD 921 million of liquidity at the quarter end, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 8.42x on derived EBITDA and thin interest cover of 1.74x. Cash-flow durability appears adequate in political years and weak in off-years because fixed costs and a shrinking fee line magnify the cycle. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on political-year earnings in 2026 and 2028, the pace of retransmission erosion and the outcome of network renewals from 2027. The primary downside path is an off-year at the 2025 earnings level before the 2028 maturities are refinanced. Further analysis would require the proxy statement, the executed credit agreement and indentures, the earnings of the acquired stations, ratings and peer data, and balance-sheet figures after 2026-06-30. Top risk: leverage that depends on political-year earnings ahead of a refinancing cluster in 2028 and 2029. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B1; calculation B3; calculation B5; calculation B6

### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and releases are sufficient to run the requested credit snapshot on Gray Media, but only on a June 2026 base and without executed debt documents, ratings or ownership detail, so every creditor-facing figure inherits those limits.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage is high and cyclical, with net debt at 8.42x derived reported EBITDA and cash interest cover of 1.74x at 2026-06-30, so creditors depend on political-year earnings recovering while no principal falls due before 2028.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 2-5, 15-16; calculation K22; calculation K23

The issuer's own covenant ratio of 5.73x looks far lower because its denominator averages eight quarters and adds acquisition and synergy adjustments, so it is not comparable with these figures. Liquidity was USD 921 million of cash and undrawn revolver at quarter end, but the derived EBITDA, the quarter-end balance-sheet date and the unquantified revolver borrowing since then limit how far these figures can be pushed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 33-37; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 12-13; calculation K30; calculation K32

### Analysis by dimension

Leverage is high and swings with the political cycle rather than with debt paydown. Total debt was 5.02x derived reported EBITDA at FY2024, 9.13x at FY2025 and 8.68x on the twelve months to 2026-06-30, while carrying-value debt moved only from USD 5,621 million to USD 5,744 million and USD 5,808 million. The swing came from EBITDA, which fell from USD 1,120 million to USD 629 million as political advertising revenue dropped from USD 497 million to USD 42 million, and recovered to USD 669 million on the twelve months to 2026-06-30 with USD 113 million of political revenue in the first half of 2026. A large share of broadcasting operating expenses is fixed, so lost political revenue falls straight through to EBITDA, and creditors should expect year-end leverage to look better or worse by several turns depending on the political calendar.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 48-49; calculation K21; calculation K2; calculation K3; calculation K6

Interest cover is thin and depends on the same cycle. Derived reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.84x in FY2024, 1.60x in FY2025 and 1.74x on the twelve months to 2026-06-30, and 1.70x and 1.84x on issuer-adjusted EBITDA for FY2025 and the twelve months. Cash interest paid of about USD 393 million in FY2025 absorbed about 62% of derived EBITDA before USD 85 million of preferred and common dividends and USD 108 million of purchases of property and equipment. Operating cash flow of USD 289 million left only USD 96 million after those uses, so the preferred dividend of USD 52 million and the capital programme are funded, but with little room for acquisitions or debt reduction in an off-year.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 75-76; calculation K23; calculation K24; calculation K25; calculation K26; calculation K28

Cash flow quality weakened and the receivables securitization behaves as debt-like funding. Operating cash flow fell from USD 751 million in FY2024 to USD 289 million in FY2025 and was USD 124 million in the first half of 2026 against USD 163 million a year earlier, with working capital contributing USD 114 million less than in the first half of 2025. The securitization had USD 400 million of receivables sold at both year-end and quarter-end, derecognised as a true sale and so absent from total debt, while the receivables kept as collateral fell from USD 344 million to USD 125 million. The facility therefore adds no further liquidity and its USD 400 million is a claim on cash flow that senior creditors should weigh beside the USD 600 million of redeemable preferred stock, together USD 1,000 million outside the debt figures.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 75-76, 78; calculation K36

Liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months on the issuer's own figures but the capital structure has a 2028 wall. Cash of USD 176 million and USD 745 million of revolver availability gave USD 921 million at 2026-06-30 against about USD 465 million of interest due over the next twelve months and no principal due before 2028, after cash fell by USD 192 million in the first half of 2026 on USD 264 million of station acquisitions. The 2028 term loan of USD 739 million and the revolver commitments both end in 2028, and USD 1,125 million of 2029 first lien notes follow, so USD 1,864 million of term loan and first lien notes comes due within two years of each other. The post-quarter acquisitions and the bond repurchase were paid from cash and revolver borrowings of amounts the issuer does not state, so liquidity after 2026-06-30 is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 15-16, 25, 34; calculation K30; calculation K20; calculation K35

The issuer's covenant ratio is not a substitute for these measures. The consolidated total net leverage ratio of 5.73x at 2026-06-30 divides USD 5,696 million of net debt by a USD 994 million denominator that averages eight quarters, whose eight-quarter total of USD 1,987 million includes USD 144 million of adjustments for acquired and divested stations, financings and expected synergies, against USD 669 million of derived twelve-month EBITDA, and the first lien test of 2.55x is far below its 4.25x limit applying when the revolver is drawn. This is the strongest contrary evidence to the high-leverage reading: if political-year EBITDA in the second half of 2026 restores the twelve-month figure towards the covenant denominator, the gap would narrow, but the filings give no basis to treat the adjustments as realised.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 35-37; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 12-13; calculation K32

Data-quality and definition risks are bounded but real. The filings print no EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is derived and adjusted EBITDA exists only in the releases, with FY2023 not printed; the third quarter of 2025 has no release in the supplied set, so the twelve-month figure is built from full-year and half-year columns. Cash interest is an approximate note figure, several statement lines print dashes or are absent from the six-month statements, and the first-quarter 2026 covenant table differs from its own debt note by USD 6 million of secured principal and USD 1 million of total principal. None of these changes the direction of the findings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_gtn20260331_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 30; EX-99.1_2026-02-26_ex_924265.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 11; calculation K37; calculation K33

Subsequent events are flagged and kept out of the period figures. The first closings of the American Spirit Media and WHPM acquisitions paid USD 43 million in cash after the quarter end, which raises net debt to USD 5,675 million and net leverage to 8.48x before any acquired EBITDA, and a repurchase of USD 120 million of 2029 and 2031 notes at par left net debt unchanged except for accrued interest not stated. A new authorisation of up to USD 250 million for debt repurchases and a pension plan termination awaiting regulatory approval do not change net debt at the balance-sheet date.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 25-26; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 4-5; calculation K31

spans.text: # Business & governance: GRAY MEDIA, INC (gtn)
## Request

GRAY MEDIA, INC (issuer gtn), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, ownership and control, transaction history and financial-policy behaviour of the issuer from the seven supplied filings and releases, with the source readiness results of this run as the only earlier input. No valuation, rating or recommendation is made.
## Sources

| EX-99.1_2026-05-07_ex_956963.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) for the first quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-05-07 | b04f43ebe7b79436fed34dc07bcf8f9f9fb0c9fac32a39299a3e02ac7ae325d8 | January and April 2026 debt repayments, credit agreement amendment, distribution dispute. |

## Findings
### Bottom line

Governance risk is medium: control sits with ten-vote Class A shares and an insider family group, not a financial sponsor, and recent policy pairs maturity extension and debt repurchases with a large acquisition programme, a debt-funded preferred repurchase and continued dividends. The holders of the votes and their percentages are not established, so creditors cannot yet test how far insider restraint protects them.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 37-38, 45; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 15, 18; calculation A1

The business is cyclical: revenue splits almost evenly between advertising and retransmission fees, and political advertising fell from USD 497 million in 2024 to USD 42 million in 2025 while adjusted EBITDA fell 42.3%, so debt service is easiest in election years.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 49, 89; EX-99.1_2026-02-26_ex_924265.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation A3; calculation A7
### Key findings

- Voting control sits with Class A holders whose identity is not established. Each Class A share carries ten votes, so the 9.58% of shares outstanding that are Class A carried 51.45% of all votes on 2026-07-31, and the filing says an insider family group can exert significant influence, with the Executive Chairman and chief executive married to a director. Creditors therefore face shareholder decisions on mergers, acquisitions and distributions that the Class A holders can carry if they vote together, and the sources give no holding percentage or board independence to test who those holders are.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 37-38, 44-45; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation A1

- Financial policy is mixed rather than extractive. Gray repurchased USD 120 million of its own notes at par in July 2026, authorised up to USD 250 million more through 2027 and, in 2025, refinanced so that no principal falls due before December 2028; against that, it paid USD 85 million of dividends in 2025, equal to 47.0% of operating cash flow after capital expenditure, and cash dividends continued in 2026.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 25-26; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_ex_956963.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 54, 75; calculation A12; calculation A16

- The June 2026 preferred repurchase is the clearest case of senior secured debt paying a junior claim in cash. Gray raised USD 70 million of additional first lien notes and used USD 30 million to retire preferred stock with a USD 50 million liquidation value, a price of 60% of face; annual cash dividends fall by USD 4 million and the new interest is smaller, but first lien debt rose while a junior claim was paid, and the other USD 40 million went to buy stations.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 18; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation A15; calculation A17

- The acquisition programme adds scale, but its credit return cannot yet be measured. Closings in the first half of 2026 cost USD 280 million, with USD 54 million more agreed, and were paid from cash on hand; the 2026 acquisitions added USD 41 million of second-quarter revenue, but purchased earnings, purchase multiples and synergies are not disclosed, and the remaining station closings need regulatory approval.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 11-13, 25, 29; 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 90; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 1-3; calculation A8; calculation A9; calculation A11

- Retransmission revenue is as large as advertising but mostly belongs to the networks, so the cash that supports debt is thinner than revenue suggests. Retransmission consent revenue was 46.2% of 2025 revenue, yet network affiliation fees took 61.7% of it, leaving USD 547 million; first-half retransmission revenue fell from USD 748 million to USD 698 million after subscriber losses, an Atlanta affiliation loss and a satellite blackout, and the Big Four affiliation agreements begin expiring in the second half of 2027.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 49-50; EX-99.1_2026-02-26_ex_924265.htm.jsonl, pages 1-2; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 3-4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation A3; calculation A6

- Fixed costs make earnings fall faster than revenue in the off-political year, which is when leverage looks worst. From 2024 to 2025 revenue fell 15.1% while adjusted EBITDA, an issuer-defined measure, fell 42.3%, because broadcasting expenses fell by only USD 78 million against a revenue fall of USD 549 million; political revenue of USD 113 million in the first half of 2026 is the first test of a recovery.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 48-50; EX-99.1_2026-02-26_ex_924265.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation A5; calculation A7

- Disclosure is adequate for monitoring but thin on the documents that set creditor rights. The auditor gave unqualified opinions on the 2025 statements and on internal control, and each release states the covenant ratios, yet the covenant earnings base of USD 1,987 million over eight quarters includes USD 184 million of acquisition, synergy and unrestricted-subsidiary adjustments, and USD 400 million of receivables have been sold through a securitization facility, behind which the secured notes rank on those assets.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 68-70, 93-94; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 37; calculation A19; calculation A21
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for lower risk is what the sources do not show: no financial sponsor, no covenant waiver or forbearance, no exchange offer or priming transaction, no fees paid to insiders and no related-party leakage appear in them, and the 2025 refinancing removed near-term maturities while the repurchases at par and the USD 250 million authorisation reduce debt. The auditor's unqualified opinions and quarterly covenant reporting add to that. These absences are not proof, because the proxy statement, the credit agreement and the indentures were not supplied. The view would move to low if the proxy statement showed a limited insider stake and a majority of independent directors and the indentures showed tight restricted-payment and unrestricted-subsidiary limits. It would move to high if the Class A votes proved to sit with one insider group and distributions, preferred repurchases or par buybacks of selected notes continued while the first lien test was tightening, or if a later filing disclosed an uptier, drop-down or non-pro-rata exchange.
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so Class A ownership, family holdings, board independence and related-party dealings are not established; any of them could move the governance risk level by itself and the view on who can force a shareholder decision.

- The executed credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so capacity for restricted payments, new debt, liens and unrestricted-subsidiary transfers is not established; the creditor-alignment reading therefore rests on observed behaviour, not on what documents permit.
- Acquired earnings, purchase multiples and synergies are not disclosed, so the acquisition finding is directional only and cannot say whether the programme lowers or raises leverage.
- Evidence ends with the filings of 2026-08-07, 90 days before the as-of date, so later closings, borrowings and repurchases are not established and could change the view on financial policy.
- No market prices for the notes bought back at par are supplied, so whether any seller was paid above market, a non-pro-rata benefit, cannot be judged.
### Company and operating model
| Feature | What the filings show | Credit relevance | Source |

| What the group is | Largest US owner of top-rated local television stations: 114 full-power markets reaching about 37% of US television households, the top-rated station in 77 of 113 measured markets, the largest Telemundo affiliate group (47 markets), a digital agency and production companies. | Scale and local news leadership support advertising pricing and retransmission bargaining; the business is a single industry. | 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 4 |

| Revenue model | 2025 revenue USD 3,095 million: core advertising 46.9%, retransmission consent 46.2%, production companies 3.5%, other 2.1%, political 1.4% (political was 13.6% of 2024 revenue). | Two pillars of similar size; political advertising swings the cycle and decides which year leverage looks worst. | 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 49 |

| Cycle and seasonality | Advertising peaks in the second and fourth quarters; political spending is heaviest in the fourth quarter of even years; Olympic and Super Bowl broadcasts move NBC and FOX or CBS stations in particular years. | Earnings are cyclical by design: odd years carry the same fixed costs on far less revenue. | 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 48 |

| Networks and markets | CBS-affiliated channels 37% of 2025 revenue, NBC 27%, FOX 14%, ABC 11%; top ten markets about 25%; largest market (Phoenix) 5%. | Diversified by market, concentrated in network renewals: agreements expire from mid-2027 to 2028-12-31. | 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 4-5 |

| Retransmission economics | Retransmission consent revenue USD 1,429 million less network affiliation fees USD 882 million leaves USD 547 million in 2025 (USD 292 million against USD 281 million in the first half of 2026). | About 62% of retransmission revenue is passed to networks, so renewals and subscriber losses hit cash flow harder than revenue. | EX-99.1_2026-02-26_ex_924265.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 4 |

| Cost structure | Main broadcasting costs are compensation, benefits, programming and network fees; a large portion is fixed. | Operating leverage is high: 89.6% of the 2025 revenue decline fell through to adjusted EBITDA. | 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 48-50 |

| Advertiser mix | Services sector 26% and automotive 17% of 2025 core advertising; no customer above 5% of broadcast advertising revenue. | No customer concentration, but the main advertiser categories are cyclical. | 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 10 |

| Perimeter change in 2026 | Stations added in 22 markets net of disposals in the first half, with six more American Spirit Media markets closing in part on 2026-07-01. | The base is being rebuilt faster than a full year of acquired earnings can be observed. | EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 12-13, 25 |
### Company profile
| Item | Detail | Source |

| Issuer | Gray Media, Inc. (ticker GTN, Class A GTN.A), formerly Gray Television, Inc.; a Georgia corporation headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia | 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 3 |

| Listing and share classes | Class A common stock (ten votes per share) and common stock (one vote per share), both listed on the New York Stock Exchange; dividends on both classes are pari passu | 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 45 |
| Latest share counts | Common stock 93,115,076 and Class A common stock 9,869,307, both as of 2026-07-31 | 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 2 |

| Ownership type | Public company with insider family influence; no financial sponsor or controlling shareholder is named in the supplied sources | 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 37-38 |
| Reporting entity | Holding company with no material independent assets; substantially all subsidiaries guarantee the debt | 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 35 |

| Executive officers | Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer; President and Co-Chief Executive Officer; Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer; Executive Vice President and Chief Legal and Development Officer; Chief Operating Officer | 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 44-45 |
| Employees | 9,165 full-time and 417 part-time at 2026-02-20; 506 full-time and 16 part-time employees at 17 stations are represented by unions | 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 20 |
| Auditor | RSM US LLP; unqualified opinions on the 2025 financial statements and on internal control over financial reporting | 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 68-70 |
| Segments | Broadcasting (USD 2,988 million of 2025 revenue) and production companies (USD 107 million) | 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 73, 89 |
| Credit ratings | Not supplied: no credit rating appears in any supplied document | Not supplied: none of the seven sources states a rating |
### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Most of the 2026 acquisition programme closed in a short window. Agreements with Scripps, Sagamore Hill, Block Communications and Allen Media were signed in the third quarter of 2025 and the WBBJ purchase was announced in December 2025. Closings between 2026-01-01 and 2026-05-15 cost USD 280 million in consideration, split between WBBJ at USD 27 million, three Allen Media stations at USD 56 million, seven Allen Media markets at USD 115 million, Block at USD 80 million and Sagamore Hill at USD 2 million; the Scripps exchange moved stations without cash and produced a USD 22 million non-cash loss. A further USD 54 million is agreed for American Spirit Media and the WHPM station, of which USD 43 million was paid on the first closings on 2026-07-01 and USD 11 million awaits regulatory approval.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 11-13, 25; EX-99.1_2026-02-26_ex_924265.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2025-09-30_gtn20250930_10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation A8; calculation A9

New debt in the period was used to refinance and, in 2026, to fund growth and a junior-claim buyback. In 2025 the group issued USD 1,150 million of second lien notes due 2032 in two steps and USD 775 million of 7.25% first lien notes due 2033, and used the proceeds to redeem the 2027 notes, repay term loans and revolver borrowings and redeem part of the 2029 notes, which left no principal due before December 2028. On 2026-06-30 it added USD 70 million of the 2033 first lien notes at par, applying USD 40 million to the first American Spirit Media closing and USD 30 million to repurchase preferred stock with a USD 50 million liquidation value. The credit agreement was amended and restated on 2026-03-31 with no change in commitments or maturities.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 91-94; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 18; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation A15; calculation A17

## Findings
### Bottom line

Gray Media's credit profile is weak to adequate: scale and liquidity are real strengths, but leverage near eight and a half times derived EBITDA and thin interest cover leave little room for an off-political year before the December 2028 maturities. Net debt was 8.42x derived twelve-month EBITDA at 2026-06-30, or 8.48x pro forma for the first station closings of 2026-07-01, and cash interest cover was 1.74x; the effect of the 2026-07-21 note repurchase on net debt is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B1; calculation B3

The support is USD 921 million of cash and undrawn revolver at 2026-06-30 and no principal due before December 2028; the largest risk is a second off-year, when political revenue falls back and retransmission revenue keeps shrinking as affiliation agreements come up for renewal from 2027.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 15-16; calculation B5; calculation B10
### Key findings

- Leverage is the binding weakness, and the issuer's own ratio understates it. The covenant ratio of 5.73x is far below the derived net leverage of 8.42x (8.48x pro forma for the first closings of 2026-07-01) because it averages eight quarters and adds acquisition, synergy and unrestricted-subsidiary adjustments; creditors should read the derived figure as the economic one and the covenant ratio as the issuer's own statistic.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation B1; calculation B13

- Interest cover is thin and will look thinner on forward interest. Cash interest cover was 1.74x on derived twelve-month EBITDA, but the issuer estimates about USD 465 million of interest over the next twelve months against USD 385 million paid in the last twelve, which would lower cover to 1.44x on the same earnings until earnings rise.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 34; calculation B3; calculation B18

- Earnings, not debt, drive the swings in leverage. Total debt to derived EBITDA went from 5.02x at FY2024 to 9.13x at FY2025 on debt that moved by only USD 123 million, because derived EBITDA fell from USD 1,120 million to USD 629 million; fixed costs carried 89.6% of the revenue fall into adjusted EBITDA, so the political calendar, not paydown, sets reported leverage.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B4; calculation B9

- Liquidity is the main support but is established only to the quarter end. Cash and undrawn revolver were USD 921 million at 2026-06-30 with no principal due before December 2028, against about USD 465 million of interest over the next twelve months; cash fell by USD 192 million in the first half of 2026 after USD 264 million of station purchases, and revolver borrowing after the quarter end is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 15, 25, 34; calculation B5; calculation B16; calculation B18

- Refinancing is the medium-term test. The USD 739 million 2028 term loan and the USD 750 million revolver commitments end on 2028-12-01, and USD 1,125 million of 2029 first lien notes (USD 1,025 million after the 2026-07-21 repurchase) fall due on 2029-07-15, so USD 1,864 million of first lien debt matures in under eight months; the issuer reports the fair value of its debt at USD 5.2 billion against USD 5.8 billion carrying value, and management says the first maturity falls after the 2028 election cycle.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 15-17, 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, page 92; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_ex_956963.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation B6; calculation B11

- Revenue durability is average: the two large lines are flat to falling and the swing line is political. First-half core advertising was flat and retransmission revenue fell from USD 748 million to USD 698 million, while political revenue went from USD 497 million in 2024 to USD 42 million in 2025; net retransmission revenue held at USD 547 million in 2025 because network fees fell with it, but those fees reset as the affiliation agreements renew from the second half of 2027.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 49, 89; EX-99.1_2026-02-26_ex_924265.htm.jsonl, pages 1-2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 29; calculation B10; calculation B15

- Free cash flow is thin outside political years and the guided 2026 uses exceed trailing earnings. Free cash flow was USD 608 million in FY2024, USD 181 million in FY2025 and USD 146 million on the last twelve months; guided 2026 interest expense, dividends, capital expenditure and cash taxes add to USD 723 million to USD 753 million, above twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 709 million, so deleveraging depends on on-year earnings exceeding the trailing level.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 5-6; calculation B7; calculation B8

- Financial policy is a moderate negative, not a strength. Dividends of USD 85 million in 2025 took 47.0% of free cash flow, a preferred repurchase was funded with first lien notes and ten-vote Class A shares control the vote; against that, USD 120 million of notes were bought back at par, which is why Business & governance rates governance risk as medium and not high.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 18, 25; calculation B7; calculation B14
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for a better view is timing. Twelve-month EBITDA includes only the first half of a political year; the issuer guides third-quarter 2026 revenue to USD 935 million to USD 965 million against USD 749 million a year earlier, with political advertising of USD 165 million to USD 185 million against USD 8 million, and net retransmission revenue rose to USD 292 million from USD 281 million in the first half. The covenant ratio of 5.73x sits 1.27x below its 7.00x incurrence limit, the first lien ratio of 2.55x is far below the 4.25x limit that applies when the revolver is drawn, and management places the first maturity after the 2028 election cycle, when earnings should be at a peak. If twelve-month derived EBITDA at the end of 2026 moved back toward the USD 1,120 million of the last political year and the 2028 maturities were refinanced early, net leverage would move toward the 4.90x seen at the end of 2024 and the view would improve. It would worsen if the next off-year repeated the USD 629 million of 2025, if retransmission revenue fell faster than network fees, or if further debt-funded distributions or a covenant-limited refinancing left less room before 2028.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 1-6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 35, 37; calculation B1; calculation B13; calculation B17
### Limitations

- Leverage, cover and free cash flow are trailing figures on derived EBITDA with no forward model, so reported leverage could move by several turns in either direction once political-year earnings enter the twelve-month base, and the weak-to-adequate view would move with it.

- No credit ratings, market prices, peer figures or executed debt documents were supplied, so market access rests on the issuer's own fair-value disclosure to a tenth of a billion and refinancing flexibility cannot be tied to what the documents permit.

- The earnings of the stations bought in 2026 are not disclosed, so the effect of the acquisition programme on leverage is directional and the downside scenario uses the 2025 base without the new stations.
- Evidence stops at the second-quarter reports, so the revolver balance and the cash position after the July repurchase and station payments are not established and could lower the liquidity support.
- Ownership percentages and board independence are not established, so the financial-policy judgement could move up or down once the proxy statement is read.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength: scale and local leadership support pricing and carriage terms. The group serves more than a hundred markets and holds the top-rated station in most measured markets, no market is above 5% of revenue and no customer is above 5% of broadcast advertising revenue, so a local shock does not reach cash flow as it would for a single-market operator.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 10

Strength: committed liquidity and a clear runway. Cash and undrawn revolver of USD 921 million and no principal due before December 2028 are nearly twice the USD 465 million of interest expected over the next twelve months, even though the securitization facility is fully drawn.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 34; calculation B5; calculation B18

Strength: on-year earnings power. In the last political year derived EBITDA was USD 1,120 million and net leverage 4.90x, so leverage falls sharply when political revenue returns, which is the mechanism behind the issuer's deleveraging plan.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B1

Strength: net retransmission revenue is holding. Retransmission fees less network fees were USD 547 million in 2025 against USD 550 million in 2024 and rose to USD 292 million from USD 281 million in the first half of 2026, which cushions the loss of subscribers.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-02-26_ex_924265.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 3-4; calculation B10

Strength: transparent, audited reporting. The auditor gave unqualified opinions and the issuer states covenant ratios every quarter, which makes monitoring practical even though the executed documents are not supplied.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

Weakness: leverage and cover leave little cushion. Net leverage of 8.42x and cover of 1.74x on derived EBITDA, and 1.44x on forward interest, mean a second off-year would test the covenant ratio and refinancing access before earnings recover.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B1; calculation B3; calculation B18
Weakness: earnings swing with the political cycle and fixed costs. Revenue fell 15.1% from 2024 to 2025 while adjusted EBITDA fell 42.3%, so a flat revenue year can still cut cash flow sharply.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B9

Weakness: retransmission revenue is eroding and its network cost is about to reset. Retransmission revenue fell 6.7% in the first half of 2026 and network fees took 61.7% of 2025 retransmission revenue, with affiliation agreements expiring from 2027 to the end of 2028.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation B10

Weakness: a refinancing cluster at the end of 2028 and the middle of 2029. USD 1,864 million of first lien term loan and notes, plus the revolver, mature within under eight months of each other, and the debt trades below book on the issuer's own fair-value estimate.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 15-17; calculation B6; calculation B11

Weakness: shareholder-first choices at high leverage. Dividends took 47.0% of free cash flow in 2025, a preferred repurchase was paid with first lien notes and ten-vote shares control the vote, so the issuer can choose payouts over paydown.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B7; calculation B14

### Company description

Gray Media owns local television stations in more than a hundred US markets that reach about 37% of US television households, with the top-rated station in most of the markets Nielsen measures, plus a small production and studio business. Revenue comes in roughly equal parts from advertising and from fees that cable, satellite and streaming distributors pay to carry its stations, and political advertising adds a large layer every second year. Retransmission contracts and network affiliation agreements run for years, which gives cash-flow visibility, but advertising is sold on short contracts and the political layer disappears in odd years, so debt service in an off-year rests on a smaller, fee-based core. The group is also changing shape: it closed station purchases of USD 280 million in the first half of 2026 and swapped stations with a peer, so the earnings base is being rebuilt faster than the filings show.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 9; calculation B15; calculation B19
### Ownership and group structure

Gray is a public company controlled through votes, not through a sponsor: ten-vote Class A shares held 51.45% of votes on 2026-07-31, and an insider family group is described as able to exert significant influence. The borrower is a holding company with no material independent assets, substantially all subsidiaries guarantee the debt, and the credit facility and the first and second lien notes are secured on substantially all assets other than real estate. Two structural claims sit outside the debt figures: USD 400 million of sold receivables that the notes rank behind, and USD 600 million of redeemable preferred stock that ranks ahead of common equity and below all debt. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk as medium because distributions, a debt-funded preferred repurchase and acquisitions coincide with high leverage, offset by par repurchases of debt and a longer maturity profile; holder identities, board independence and the executed documents are not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 18, 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 37-38, 93-94; calculation B20
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Volume is set by audience share and by the number of distributor subscribers, and price by the rates in retransmission contracts and advertising rate cards. Retransmission rates rise with each renewal, but subscriber losses, an Atlanta affiliation change and a satellite blackout from March to May 2026 contributed to a USD 50 million fall in first-half retransmission revenue; core advertising was flat and carries two cyclical categories, services at 26% and automotive at 17% of 2025 core advertising. Revenue is therefore cyclical, partly structurally declining in its fee line and not concentrated by customer or market; the consequence is that pricing power exists in carriage negotiations but is being spent offsetting subscriber decline, which limits growth in the cash that supports debt.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 10, 49; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 29; 10-Q_2026-03-31_gtn20260331_10q.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation B10
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Network affiliation fees, compensation, benefits and programming are the main costs, and a large portion is fixed. The result is operating leverage: from 2024 to 2025 broadcasting expenses fell only USD 78 million against a USD 549 million fall in revenue, and adjusted EBITDA fell 42.3%. Margins can be partly defended through network fees, which fell USD 50 million in 2025 and fell further in the first half of 2026 as an Atlanta station went independent, but not against a political-year swing, so margin resilience is weak across the cycle and adequate within it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gtn20251231_10k.htm.jsonl, pages 48-50; EX-99.1_2026-02-26_ex_924265.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation B9
### Capital intensity and cash flow conversion

Capital intensity is low outside construction: purchases of property and equipment were USD 108 million in 2025, USD 104 million over the last twelve months, and the issuer guides USD 120 million to USD 130 million for 2026. Conversion of EBITDA to free cash flow is volatile, with free cash flow of USD 608 million in FY2024, USD 181 million in FY2025 and USD 146 million over the last twelve months, because cash interest of about USD 385 million and cash taxes absorb most of an off-year's EBITDA. Capital expenditure could be cut in a downside, which is a lever, but the guided 2026 uses of interest, dividends, capital expenditure and taxes of USD 723 million to USD 753 million already exceed trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 709 million.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 5-6; calculation B3; calculation B7; calculation B8
### Competitive forces

Rivalry from cable networks, streaming and digital platforms takes advertising and audience, and cord cutting removes the subscribers who generate fees, so rivalry works on both revenue lines; local news and sports programming are the issuer's response. Distributors have bargaining power, shown by the March to May 2026 satellite blackout, while networks hold supplier power over 61.7% of retransmission revenue through affiliation fees. New entry is limited by scarce licences, but substitutes are close: advertisers can move spend to digital platforms, and viewers to streaming. The credit consequence is that pricing power in the fee line is shared with networks and contested by distributors, so net retransmission revenue is a more reliable guide to cash flow than gross revenue.
### Macro and regulatory factors

Two outside factors matter. Regulation shapes deleveraging: station acquisitions need regulatory approval, the national audience cap is 39%, a court vacated the top-four ownership restriction in 2025 and the ownership review remains open, so rule changes could widen or narrow the room for further duopoly deals. The economy matters through advertising: core advertising was flat in the first half of 2026 with the issuer citing macroeconomic softness, and the risk factors name trade policy as a threat to advertiser budgets. Other factors, such as technology, are not a primary credit driver on the evidence supplied.
### Credit SWOT

- Strengths: scale across many markets; USD 921 million of cash and undrawn revolver; no principal due before December 2028; net retransmission revenue of USD 547 million that has held; audited reporting.
- Weaknesses: net leverage of 8.42x on derived EBITDA; cover of 1.74x, lower on forward interest; fixed costs that make EBITDA swing; ten-vote control and a record of distributions at high leverage.

- Opportunities: on-year political revenue; duopoly acquisitions and cost sharing if approvals and prices allow; par repurchases of debt under a USD 250 million authorisation; an early refinancing of the 2028 term loan.

- Threats: a second off-year at the 2025 earnings level; retransmission erosion and network fee resets from 2027; carriage disputes; a refinancing in 2028 or 2029 at higher cost or with less room under the covenants.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B1; calculation B3; calculation B5; calculation B10
### Financial profile and credit quality

The financial profile is weaker than the business profile. The main supports are scale, committed liquidity of USD 921 million at the quarter end, a clear runway to December 2028 and on-year earnings power, shown by net leverage of 4.90x at the end of the last political year. The main constraints are leverage of 8.42x and cover of 1.74x, free cash flow that fell from USD 608 million to USD 181 million between 2024 and 2025, margins that are fragile across the cycle because adjusted EBITDA fell 42.3% on a 15.1% revenue decline, and a financial policy that keeps paying dividends and has funded a preferred repurchase with first lien notes while also buying back debt. Capital-market access is not tested by a ratings view or market prices, and the issuer's own fair-value estimate puts the debt below carrying value. The trend is improving in 2026 as political revenue arrives, from a weak 2025 base, and the missing datapoints are the revolver balance and cash after 2026-06-30, the earnings of the acquired stations, ownership percentages and the executed debt documents.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 15-17; calculation B1; calculation B5; calculation B7; calculation B9; calculation B11
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months, 2026 is a political year, so revenue and earnings should rise: the issuer guides third-quarter revenue to USD 935 million to USD 965 million, and 2027 is an off-year when political revenue falls back and the derived leverage figures will look worst again. The tailwinds are political spending, acquisitions that add stations in markets where the group is already strong, and lower network fees; the headwinds are subscriber losses, carriage disputes, higher cash interest after the 2025 refinancing and affiliation renewals from the second half of 2027. Over three to five years the issuer's ability to refinance the 2028 and 2029 maturities in the 2028 political year, at market rates that are not known today, and to turn acquisitions into lower leverage will decide credit quality; ownership-rule changes could help but are unresolved.
### Downside scenario

The downside is a second off-year that repeats the conditions of 2025. The initiating condition is political revenue falling back from USD 113 million in the first half of 2026 toward the USD 42 million of 2025, with retransmission revenue still falling and no new carriage gains. The first break is operational: fixed costs mean that a revenue fall of 15.1% cut adjusted EBITDA by 42.3% in 2025. The financial transmission follows from the 2025 outcome: derived EBITDA of USD 629 million against cash interest of USD 393 million is cover of 1.60x and total debt to EBITDA of 9.13x, and free cash flow of USD 181 million less USD 85 million of dividends leaves USD 96 million. Liquidity does not break in this scenario, because cash flow stays positive after dividends and USD 921 million of cash and undrawn revolver and no principal before December 2028 remain, so the consequence falls on leverage and refinancing: the 2028 and 2029 maturities would then be refinanced from a weak base, with the first lien test at 2.55x still far below its limit. Management levers are cutting capital expenditure, suspending the common dividend of USD 33 million a year, and using the USD 250 million repurchase authorisation selectively; the preferred dividend of USD 50 million a year is mandatory unless paid in kind, which blocks junior distributions. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity event through 2027 on this evidence, not to avoid a harder refinancing, and the scenario uses the pre-acquisition perimeter because purchased earnings are not disclosed.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_gtn20260630_10q.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 18, 35; EX-99.1_2026-08-07_ex_998938.htm.jsonl, pages 5-6; calculation B3; calculation B4; calculation B5; calculation B7; calculation B9; calculation B12
### Overall credit view

Overall, Gray Media presents a strong-in-scale but cyclical business profile supported by local market leadership, a long runway to its first maturity and USD 921 million of liquidity at the quarter end, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 8.42x on derived EBITDA and thin interest cover of 1.74x. Cash-flow durability appears adequate in political years and weak in off-years because fixed costs and a shrinking fee line magnify the cycle. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on political-year earnings in 2026 and 2028, the pace of retransmission erosion and the outcome of network renewals from 2027. The primary downside path is an off-year at the 2025 earnings level before the 2028 maturities are refinanced. Further analysis would require the proxy statement, the executed credit agreement and indentures, the earnings of the acquired stations, ratings and peer data, and balance-sheet figures after 2026-06-30. Top risk: leverage that depends on political-year earnings ahead of a refinancing cluster in 2028 and 2029.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B1; calculation B3; calculation B5; calculation B6

- Low: no credit ratings, market prices or peer figures are supplied, so market access is read from the issuer's fair-value estimate and the business profile is not benchmarked against peers.
- Low: the executed credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so covenant capacity and recovery are not assessed here.
- Low: the earnings of the stations acquired in 2026 are not disclosed, so no pro forma leverage on acquired earnings is given.
- Low: no filing after 2026-08-07 is supplied, so the revolver balance, cash and interest effect of the July repurchase and the outcome of the pending station approvals are not established.
